items.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: when you left ‘Trane, McCoy Tyner had also left.

ctx.x: And we did that first piece, “Putting It Together”.

Yeah, I have that recording here. Let me just backtrack a little bit, you mentioned Jimmy Garrison, he had already left ‘Trane too. Let’s talk about, when you left ‘Trane, McCoy Tyner had also left. Was that something that you and he discussed?

I don’t know. I didn’t discuss my business with anybody. I don’t know…cause first of all Alice wanted to play, so that might have been good reason for McC0y to leave. She was, after all, closer to him than McCoy (Laughs). She’d say, “Honey, I want to play tomorrow.” (Laughs)

items.title: Tyner McCoy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I really didn’t know Elvin that well. I think I heard him on record but in terms of playing with him, no, I liked what I had heard on the recordings but I didn’t really meet him or play with him.

ctx.x: You already knew John, so is this your first encounter with Elvin?

John knew Elvin. I think he played with Elvin when he was with Miles or something, there was some kind of connection there and he told us about him. I’m pretty sure he discussed him with Jimmy. He liked Elvin’s playing because it was loose and it let him do things rhythmically and harmonically. Elvin had Thad in his life, so he had all that music, Elvin came out of such a musical environment it was unbelievable; so he was perfect for the band. He would go with you in whatever you were doing rhythmically or…
Definitely a sympatico between you and Elvin.
